Add `context_settings` parameter to `CliRunner.invoke`

This PR adds a `context_settings` parameter to `CliRunner.invoke()`, allowing tests to pass context-specific settings to the command's `Context`.

`CliRunner.invoke()` passes its extra keyword arguments to the `Context` of the command, except `color`: its own `color` parameter takes that name. `context_settings` solves this collision. And now a test can set what its terminal supports, as well as the `color` of the context in the same call.

With this addition, I can now test cases that were previously difficult or impossible to cover, such as verifying how the command behaves with different `Context` settings.

This was proposed 5 years ago in #2110 but at that time this change was evaluated as niche. Since then, we did a lot of color handling improvements in Click (#3505, #3653, #3739) which added a lot of color-related tests, so this is no longer a niche concern.

For evidence, I used the new `context_settings` parameter to extend and simplify existing checks. See `test_prompt_and_confirm_ansi_respects_color` and `test_tempfile_pager_handles_ansi`.

Fix spooled stream write compatibility and backwards text seeks

## The change

Make spooled streams return their write count, and let SpooledBytesIO accept buffer-protocol inputs. Wrapping the binary stream in `io.BufferedWriter` currently fails on flush because it supplies a memoryview; successful writes also return None instead of their byte or character count. The rollover calculation now uses the buffer size in bytes, including multi-byte memoryviews.

A second fix corrects backwards character-relative seeks in SpooledStringIO and rejects negative absolute destinations without moving the stream. Previously a backwards seek consumed the rest of the buffer while reporting the requested earlier position. UTF-8 navigation now restarts from the beginning for backwards movement.

Six write regression cases and six seek regression cases fail before their respective fixes. All 685 combined tests and module doctests pass afterward on Python 3.11.15. Coverage includes rolled and in-memory streams, Unicode character counts, BufferedWriter flushes, and rollover with a multi-byte memoryview. Documentation examples are updated for the returned values.

## The backstory

This follows the utility-library investigation in #502. The bug was found through source inspection and a real BufferedWriter integration regression, rather than a production incident. The change keeps spooled streams compatible with standard I/O callers.

Expose combined `__annotations__` on composed functions (#496)

`Compose` already synthesizes `__signature__` (parameters of the first function applied, return annotation of the last), but it had no `__annotations__`, so `typing.get_type_hints()` and tools that read `__annotations__` directly saw nothing on a composed callable.

This adds an instance property that builds the same view:

```python
def f(x: int) -> str: ...
def g(y: str) -> float: ...
compose(g, f).__annotations__          # {'x': int, 'return': float}
typing.get_type_hints(compose(g, f))   # {'x': int, 'return': float}
```

Functions without annotations contribute nothing; callables with no `__annotations__` at all (e.g. `str`, arbitrary objects) are handled.

Scope: this is a small runtime step toward the static typing discussed in #496 — the composed callable now reports `Callable[[A], C]` for `compose(g, f)` with `f: A -> B`, `g: B -> C`. It does not add stubs or annotate the library itself; happy to split or drop it if you'd rather approach #496 differently.

Tests: `test_compose_annotations` (combined view, unannotated pieces, `get_type_hints`, consistency with `__signature__`). Full suite incl. doctests passes locally (`pytest --doctest-modules toolz/`; the only failure is `test_has_version`, which needs an installed distribution and fails identically on master in my environment).

Fix numeric_range equality and hashing above sys.maxsize

### Issue reference

Closes #1344.

### Changes

Use `numeric_range._len`, its cached arbitrary-precision length, when comparing or hashing numeric ranges. Calling `len()` internally currently raises `OverflowError` for otherwise valid ranges whose number of values exceeds `sys.maxsize`. This prevents equality comparisons and use as dictionary keys, whereas the built-in `range` supports both.

The explicit public call `len(numeric_range(10**30))` continues to raise `OverflowError`, like `len(range(10**30))`; this change does not alter that API behavior.

Regression tests cover equal ranges (including different stops yielding the same values), descending ranges, unequal lengths/starts/steps, matching built-in range hashes, and dictionary lookups using an equivalent range.

### Checks and tests

Validation on Windows / CPython 3.13.9 against master 08dca28:
- Before the fix, the new regression tests produce nine failing subcases with `OverflowError`.
- Full unittest suite under coverage: **936 tests run, OK (5 skipped)**; **100% coverage** (2,233 statements).

fix: validate the chunk size in chunked_even

### Issue reference

N/A — trivial boundary fix; no issue was filed.

### Changes

`chunked_even(iterable, n)` did not validate `n` before handing it to `islice`. A negative size leaked `ValueError: Indices for islice()...`; a zero size leaked `ValueError: Step for islice()...` and consumed two source items before raising. Its sibling sizing functions (`chunked`, `ichunked`, `sliced`) already define the contract: `n == 0` yields nothing without consuming the source, `n < 0` raises `ValueError('n must be at least 0')`.

The fix adds those two guards at the top of `chunked_even`, before `iter(iterable)`, so invalid sizes fail before any source consumption and match the rest of the module.

The new `test_zero_chunk_size` and `test_negative_chunk_size` fail on `4aeb433` with the `islice` errors and pass on this branch. They also assert the source iterator is untouched after the error/empty result.

peekable: avoid caching entire iterable on negative slice with omitted stop

### Issue reference
None

### Changes
A reverse slice with an omitted stop, such as `peekable(count())[5::-1]`, ends at index 0. The old implementation treated the internal negative stop sentinel as right-relative indexing and cached the entire source. This hangs on an infinite iterator and buffers unnecessary items on a large finite source.

Cache only through `start + 1` for this case; retain full caching for actual negative indices or an omitted reverse start. The release note is under Unreleased, above the existing 11.2.1/11.2.0 history.

_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRAsyLfisvwRS6VXWYtrwRWi)_

Fixes #763.

Before: `unregister()` left the plugin in `list_plugin_distinfo()` / `list_plugin_distributions()` (and so in pytest's "plugins:" header), and reloading the entry point appended a duplicate row.

After: both listings only show entry-point plugins that are still registered, and a reload takes the old slot.

How: the private `_plugin_distinfo` list of `(plugin, dist)` tuples becomes `_name2dist: dict[str, Distribution]`, keyed by the registration name like `_name2plugin`. `unregister()` pops the name; the listings are built from the two dicts, so no identity map over plugin objects is needed. `list_plugin_distinfo()` now just wraps `list_plugin_distributions()`.

The `_name2plugin` cleanup in `unregister()` becomes `if not self.is_blocked(name): pop`. The old guard existed only to keep a blocked name's marker, and the `assert name is not None` was a leftover mypy narrowing from 2019. `test_unregister_blocked` now asserts the block survives, which it did not check before.

Restore autospec calls to @cachedmethod decorated methods

# Description

On class access, `@cachedmethod` methods now return a small callable object
instead of a plain function. Calling through the class, as in
`Cached.get(obj, 1)`, still works as before.

## Motivation and Context

Since v7.2.2, calling a `@cachedmethod` method on an autospec mock raises
`TypeError: missing a required argument`. See #443 for a reproduction.

`create_autospec()` drops `self` only from plain functions in the class
`__dict__`. Here that entry is the descriptor, so mock takes whatever class
access returns as the instance-call signature. Since v7.2.2 that is a function
with signature `(self, key)`, so the first argument is bound to `self`.

The fix returns a callable object instead, so mock checks calls against its
`__call__(self, /, *args, **kwargs)`. `functools.update_wrapper()` keeps
`__wrapped__`, `__name__` and `__qualname__`, so `inspect.signature(Cached.get)`
is unchanged.

Behavior notes:

- Autospec mocks accept any arguments for these methods, as they did in v7.2.1.
  Exact parity with undecorated methods isn't possible while the class
  attribute is a descriptor.
- In v7.2.1, autospec mocks also had `cache_clear`, `cache_info` and the other
  wrapper attributes. Since v7.2.2 they don't, and this PR does not bring them
  back.
- Calling through the class without an instance still raises `TypeError`, with
  a different message.

## Related Issue

https://github.com/tkem/cachetools/issues/443

## Has this been tested and documented?

`tox` passes (py, docs, doctest, pyright, ruff, ruff-format).

regression.

Fix #435: Restore class access to cached instance methods

# Description

Restore calls to a `cachedmethod` through its class when the instance is explicitly supplied: `Example.value(example, 3)` now uses the same per-instance wrapper as `example.value(3)`.

Class access currently creates a wrapper bound to `None`, so evaluating the cache factory raises `AttributeError`. The shared descriptor now returns an unbound callable which binds the supplied instance through the existing descriptor. Locking, condition handling and per-instance statistics continue to use the existing wrappers. The original method remains available as `__wrapped__`.

## Motivation and Context

This ordinary instance-method invocation worked in cachetools 6.2.0 and fails on current master. It is separate from the deprecated `@classmethod` behavior.

fix(withoutBase): collapse leading slashes

slicing the base prefix from inputs like `/legacy//evil.com` left the
remainder as `//evil.com`, which browsers interpret as a protocol-relative
URL. This enabled an open redirect when consumers (e.g. nitro route rules)
fed the result into a redirect Location header.

Normalize all leading slashes on the trimmed remainder so the output is
always a single-host-relative path.




## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Enhanced path sanitization to prevent potential security vulnerabilities with protocol-relative URLs. Malformed paths containing repeated leading slashes are now safely normalized to relative path formats.

* **Tests**
  * Added test coverage for edge cases with repeated leading slashes in paths.

fix(withBase, withoutBase): prevent false prefix matches

Resolves: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/33924

## Summary

While investigating [nuxt/nuxt#33924](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/33924), I found that `withoutBase` was being a bit too eager when stripping base URLs.

**The issue:** When using `baseURL: '/admin/'` with a page like `/admin-dashboard`, the function incorrectly stripped `/admin` because it only checked `startsWith()` without verifying that the match ends at a path segment boundary.

```js
withoutBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin/")
// Before: "/-dashboard" ❌
// After:  "/admin-dashboard" ✅
```

The fix: Added a simple check to ensure the character after the base is either /, ?, or end of string before treating it as a valid base match.

Test plan

- Added test cases for the bug
- All existing tests pass

### Update ⚠️
Same issue is in `withBase` as well. I also fixed it and added new tests.
